case_name: Neumec Developers and Builders v. Homebuyers (Second Appeals)
citation: Bombay High Court, order dated 5 August 2026
holding_summary: Justice N.J. Jamadar dismissed two second appeals filed by Neumec Developers, holding that a promoter cannot have its delay-condonation application considered without first making the mandatory pre-deposit under Section 43(5) of RERA - a delay application is part of the appeal itself and cannot be treated as a separate, independent application for this purpose.
why_it_matters: Developers cannot sidestep RERA's mandatory pre-deposit requirement by first seeking condonation of delay in filing an appeal - the pre-deposit obligation attaches from the outset of the appeal.

case_name: M/s Avon Elastomers v. M/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance and Ors.
citation: Supreme Court of India, order dated 13 August 2026
holding_summary: A Bench of Justices K.V. Viswanathan and Arun Palli flagged anomalies in how consumer fora's pecuniary jurisdiction is fixed - by the value of goods/services/consideration paid rather than the compensation claimed - and directed the Union of India to file an affidavit within six weeks explaining the basis for reducing the National Commission's pecuniary jurisdiction from Rs. 10 crore (under the 2019 Act) to Rs. 2 crore by a December 2021 notification. Listed for further hearing on 8 October 2026.
why_it_matters: A pending, high-profile Supreme Court reference could reshape which consumer forum (District/State/National) has jurisdiction over high-value claims where the price paid is modest but the compensation sought is large - worth tracking for any consumer-facing client with a pending or contemplated complaint.

case_name: In re: Front-of-Pack Labelling for HFSS Foods - Supreme Court Supervision (September 2026 Hearing)
citation: Supreme Court of India, order dated 10 September 2026
holding_summary: In the ongoing FoPL supervision matter, FSSAI's 28 August 2026 affidavit proposed a two-phase rollout of interpretive 'red hexagon' warning labels - Phase 1 covering products high in two or more nutrients of concern (plus specified sweetened beverages), Phase 2 extending to products high in any single nutrient. On 10 September 2026 the Supreme Court questioned this phased, multi-nutrient-first approach and how ultra-processed foods would be treated relative to other packaged foods, directing the Centre and FSSAI to file further affidavits within 10 days; next listed 28 September 2026.
why_it_matters: The scope and timeline of India's mandatory front-of-pack warning label regime remains in flux - packaged food manufacturers should track the 28 September hearing before finalising label redesigns or compliance timelines.

case_name: Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Co. Ltd. v. JSW Energy Ltd. (Ratnagiri)
citation: Appeal from APTEL order dated 19 August 2026; Supreme Court of India (pending)
court: Supreme Court of India (on appeal from the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity)
holding_summary: APTEL dismissed MSEDCL's appeal against a MERC order that had directed MSEDCL to pay JSW Energy's Ratnagiri plant roughly Rs. 600 crore in tariff and late-payment-surcharge dues under a 2010 power purchase agreement, and refused MSEDCL leave to file a review petition. MSEDCL escalated the dispute to the Supreme Court, which agreed to hear the matter urgently; of the disputed amount, about Rs. 250 crore has already been paid to JSW Energy as interim relief under an earlier Supreme Court order, and the MERC order continues to operate pending the Supreme Court's hearing.
why_it_matters: A large, still-unresolved tariff and late-payment-surcharge dispute between a major private generator and a state discom is headed for final adjudication at the Supreme Court - worth tracking for any power generator or discom with PPA-linked payment disputes before MERC/APTEL.

case_name: In Re: Pay and Allowances of the Members of the Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions (Suo Motu)
citation: Supreme Court of India, order dated 13 August 2026
holding_summary: In suo motu proceedings on the pay and allowances of consumer commission members, a Bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant (with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohan) flagged a 'quality crisis' and mounting arrears across district, state, and national consumer fora, remarking that consumer commissions cannot function as rehabilitation posts for retired judges and bureaucrats. The Court directed the NCDRC President to file a status report on total pendency, filings, and disposal rates, and floated the need for regional/circuit benches to ease the backlog.
why_it_matters: A pan-India performance review of consumer commissions is now underway at the Supreme Court's direction - litigants and businesses with pending consumer complaints should expect scrutiny of, and potentially structural changes to, how quickly district/state/national consumer fora dispose of cases.

case_name: Manav Bhanot v. National Highway Authority of India
holding_summary: In a National Highways Act, 1956 land acquisition where the Competent Authority first determined compensation in July 2014, the Supreme Court held that solatium, interest and interest on solatium are payable under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 rather than the 2013 Right to Fair Compensation Act, because the deciding date is when the Competent Authority's Section 3G(1) determination (the equivalent of a Collector's award) was first made -- not the date of the underlying notification or a later arbitral award. The Court allowed the appeal to the extent of directing that the arbitral award's compensation be supplemented with 1894 Act solatium and interest, and remanded computation and disbursal to the Competent Authority.
why_it_matters: Settles which statute's solatium/interest rates apply to NH Act highway acquisitions straddling the 1 January 2015 cut-off, giving landowners and NHAI a clear, litigation-tested rule keyed to the date of the original compensation determination rather than any later arbitration or appeal.

case_name: High Point Supply Company LLC v. Agati Healthcare Private Limited
citation: Commercial First Appeal No. 15 of 2026, Bombay High Court, order dated August 2026
holding_summary: A Division Bench of Justices R.I. Chagla and Farhan P. Dubash set aside a trial court order that had rejected a US-based distributor's commercial suit against its Indian supplier for want of pre-institution mediation under Section 12-A of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, and restored the suit. The Bench clarified that whether a suit 'contemplates urgent interim relief' -- the statutory exception to mandatory pre-institution mediation -- calls for only a limited jurisdictional inquiry, not an assessment of the suit's merits or the likelihood of the interim relief actually being granted, and that seeking monetary relief alongside urgent reliefs does not by itself defeat the exception.
why_it_matters: Gives commercial litigants a clearer, merits-blind test for invoking the urgent-interim-relief exception to Section 12-A mediation, reducing the risk that a suit seeking both damages and injunctive relief gets thrown out at the threshold for skipping mediation.
